html:
Kimpa Vita, baptised Dona Beatriz, was a young noblewoman of the kingdom of Kongo who in 1704 began preaching that Saint Anthony spoke through her. Her movement, called Antonianism, tried to reunite the kingdom and make its Christianity African. She was burned as a heretic in 1706.

Kongo had been Catholic since its king was baptised in 1491. But after the Battle of Mbwila in 1665, where the Portuguese killed the king, the kingdom fell into civil war and the old capital, São Salvador, was left in ruins.

Kimpa Vita taught that Jesus had been born in São Salvador and that the saints were Kongolese. She called on the rival kings to reoccupy the capital and end the wars, and thousands of followers went to live in its ruins. She rejected the authority of the Italian Capuchin missionaries. King Pedro IV had her captured, and with the friars' approval she was burned at the stake.

Pedro went on to reunite Kongo by 1709. Kimpa Vita is remembered as an early African Christian prophet, and later movements such as that of Simon Kimbangu are often compared to hers.
